messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGE: KV cache QPS spike detected on prod-cluster-3, service=runtime, symptom=continuous-batching backlog increase > 5x, estimated impact: elevated p95 token latency and some 503s. @oncall:maya, severity=P2.

maya: acked. jumping in — oncall (maya) taking lead. logging into infra. anyone seeing customer tickets? @support-bot? :eyes:

support-bot: seeing a handful of customer errors in the last 12m — mostly streaming timeouts and a couple 502s from gen endpoint. Customer impact: intermittent failures for 4 customers, increased latencies for others.

alex: I see spike in continuous batch queue lengths on instances serving prefix cache. CPU and mem steady but KV read latency went from ~3ms to ~40-120ms on a subset of nodes.

maya: interesting — could be a hot key or cache churn. alex, can you dump top keys? also add `--verbose` to kv client logs.

alex: running quick agg: `SELECT key,count(*) FROM kv_reads WHERE ts>now()-5m GROUP BY key ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20` — top keys include several prompt-prefix hashes with similar templates. sending sample in a sec.

(dani uploaded): ```
# sample top hot keys
prefix_hash:abcd1234 -> 252k reads
prefix_hash:abcf9999 -> 198k reads
prefix_hash:abce0001 -> 185k reads
```

li: those hashes map back to two different tokenizer versions. we rolled tokenizer v2 to canary yesterday — might be a mismatch causing extra key proliferation (template drift + hash churn).

maya: okay that aligns with hypothesis. mitigation plan: 1) throttle KV read hotspotting by enabling per-prefix rate-limiter (soft) 2) revert continuous batching config to safe baseline on prod-cluster-3 3) roll back tokenizer canary on serving tier if we confirm mapping mismatch. any objections?

alex: initiating config change to batching: ```
# currently
batching.window_ms=50
batching.max_inflight=200
# temp mitigation
batching.window_ms=10
batching.max_inflight=80
``` applying to slice-4 now.

infra-runner: deploy started to slice-4. rolling in 2-min waves. will monitor for queue length improvement.

maya: enabling soft per-prefix TL on router: 50r/s for top-100 prefixes to avoid thundering herd. doing that now.

(dogfooder-bot): system: router policy applied to prod-cluster-3 (policy id: r-policy-202403).

alex: after batching change and TL, queues dropped ~65% on slice-4 within 90s, p95 token latency down from 420ms to 160ms. good so far.

maya: great. li — can you validate tokenizer mapping and confirm whether v2 produced different prefix hashing? if yes we need to stop the rollout and reconcile key namespace.

li: confirmed. tokenizer v2 changed whitespace normalization which altered prompt hashing for templates with variable whitespace. the hash function is stable but input differs -> new keys. this produced sudden spike as many requests create new prefixes instead of hitting cached entries.

maya: so root cause = tokenizer mismatch + template drift -> cache cardinality explosion -> continuous batching backlog -> degraded latencies and some 503s.

dani: any customers affected with sensitive data? support-bot said 4 customers saw errors but no PII leaks.

maya: okay. next steps: rollback tokenizer canary from serving tier immediately, kick a background scrub to consolidate identical templates (normalize whitespace) in prefixing logic as short-term patch, create PR for long-term: versioned prefix keys (tokenizer-version in key) and safer rollout gating.

alex: rolling back tokenizer v2 on prod-serving canaries now. ETA ~7m.

infra-runner: rollback finished on canaries. observing further reduction in new prefix creation. overall cache miss-rate trending down.

maya: good. I'll open a pagerduty incident ticket with summary and customer impact. tagging SRE and runtime teams for postmortem.

support-bot: customer outreach: SEs notified customers, offered incident explanation and mitigation steps. logs/trace links: https://redwood.internal/trace/xyz (internal).

maya: quick customer impact assessment: severity P2, ~4 customers saw errors for ~16 minutes peak window, bulk saw elevated latency for ~30 minutes. No data exfiltration.

li: patch idea to avoid repeating: add tokenizer-version header into prefix key derivation and include a migration shim that treats old/new keys as equivalent for N minutes during rollout. also add metric alert when unique prefix count increases > 3x in 5m.

dani: +1 to the alert. I'll file an infra ticket for rate-limiter as config knob per deployment so we can toggle quickly.

maya: oncall handoff: I’m handing off to @alex for the overnight watch. alex — owner for immediate follow-ups, li for tokenizer & prefix migration plan, dani for infra rate-limiter and alerts, maya primary incident lead + PM comms.

alex: taking over. I’ll keep an eye for any re-surge and run a background consolidation job to merge near-duplicate prefixes.

pagerduty-bot: NOTE: incident acknowledged by alex. incident status: Mitigated -> monitoring.

maya: postmortem owners assigned: li (root cause + fix), alex (operational mitigation + consolidation job), dani (alerts + TL-as-a-feature). I'll schedule a follow-up async postmortem doc and ops runbook updates.

support-bot: closing customer-facing communication: template drafted, ready for review by maya.

maya: thanks team. final note: we avoided wide-scale outage but this is a near-miss for cache churn at scale — let's treat as high priority for runbook and rollout gating. :lock:
